clue.text: They listen and look out for the fiddles

definitions.meaning: ... in the old sense are hearers, people in an audience
accountants who inspect the books watch for fraud, a fiddle being a swindle

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: hearers of a speech, and accountants checking company books for fraud.

clue.text: It finds it difficult to keep in shape

definitions.text: It finds it difficult to keep in shape

parts.words: It finds it difficult to keep in shape
parts.note: reads like a dieter, but describes a single-celled creature that constantly changes its outline

explanation.definitionFit: This microscopic organism has no fixed form and keeps altering its outline as it moves.

clue.text: Period just short of 26 years? Sounds bad

indicators.note: signals that a word for bad is said aloud to give the answer's spelling

parts.note: food gone bad has decayed

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that a stretch of almost twenty-six years sounds dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: '26' points to the answer at 26-across, a number one more than ten, so a span just short of that many years is ten years.
explanation.definitionFit: A span of ten years is a common measure of time, the period described.

clue.text: This concoction is neat

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture made up from ingredients, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink described as taken straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a herbal infusion is a concoction, and its letters are a mix of IS NEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal tea is an infusion, a brewed concoction of leaves or flowers.

clue.text: Where to grow up?

parts.note: seems to ask about childhood, but means a place to cultivate plants high up on top of a building

explanation.definitionFit: A planted area on top of a building is literally where things grow up high.

clue.text: Nice language

parts.note: looks like polite speech, but Nice is the city on the Riviera, so this is the tongue spoken there

explanation.definitionFit: The city of Nice lies in France, where the national tongue is spoken.

clue.text: Belonging nowhere and, reportedly, without a map

indicators.note: signals that a phrase is heard spoken rather than read, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: a traveller with no map has no route, so is routeless

explanation.surface: A drifter who has no home and no map either.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no roots means having no settled home or ties to any community.

clue.text: Our men mixed with American divers

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of these two words are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A team of British men joined by American scuba divers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is not people diving but the old adjective meaning several or many.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers as an adjective means various or many in number, a synonym.

clue.text: You can't bank on some rest

definitions.text: You can't bank on some rest

parts.words: You can't bank on some rest
parts.note: sounds like breaks are unreliable, but refers to days off that are not bank ..., the British public days off

explanation.definitionFit: Breaks from work, some of which are not public bank days off, so cannot be banked on.

clue.text: See 10
Academic event: time for the glad rags

parts.note: academic in the sense of theoretical or conventional can mean formal
an event is an occasion

explanation.surface: A university function where everyone dresses up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glad rags' is British slang for one's best clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressy function is the moment for putting on your best clothes.

clue.text: Banter, they say, is not good when you're old

parts.note: something not good is bad
when old you are advanced in age, so in age

explanation.surface: A remark that joking chatter is unbecoming in the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' attaches to the definition: banter, as people call it; the rest splits as bad in age.
explanation.definitionFit: Light teasing conversation is a synonym of playful chat.

clue.text: Silly Alfred exploded

indicators.note: silly suggests the name is behaving foolishly, so its letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A foolish man named Alfred lost his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To flare up is to burst out suddenly, as in a fit of temper.

clue.text: Twister has ruined his garment

indicators.note: ruined means these words are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A tornado wrecked a man's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose cotton top worn for sport is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Victoria's favourite interest: a dream state

parts.note: John Brown was Queen Victoria's favoured Scottish servant
a study is a subject of interest

explanation.surface: A queen's hobby described as a state of reverie.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means a mood of deep, absent-minded thought, a daydreaming state.

clue.text: What a lover may do to X

definitions.text: What a lover may do to X

parts.words: What a lover may do to X
parts.note: X is the symbol for a kiss, so a lover may plant one, a formal verb for kissing

explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for kissing, and X stands for a kiss at the end of letters.

clue.text: Sweetheart unhappy over lute

indicators.note: unhappy suggests the letters are disturbed and fall into a different order

explanation.surface: A lover saddened by a lute, the old instrument of serenades.
explanation.definitionFit: One's beloved is called a sweetheart, a term of endearment.

clue.text: Cosy place where the heads of French Intelligence live

indicators.note: heads means the first letters of the two following words

parts.note: to live somewhere is to reside

explanation.surface: French spy chiefs living somewhere comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: The area by the hearth is a warm and snug spot in a home.

clue.text: Soldier, priest, or maker of tableware?

definitions.meaning: a soldier is a member of the armed services
a priest is a man who takes church services
a service is a set of crockery, so playfully its maker

explanation.definitionFit: A soldier is one in the forces; the other two are whimsical readings of services.

clue.text: The City wrapped in comfort still

indicators.note: wrapped in means one word is put inside another

parts.note: balm is something soothing, a comfort
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: London's financial district snug and still comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' is a verb here: to quieten.
explanation.definitionFit: To still the wind or a ship is to calm it, a synonym.

clue.text: A bank's religious premises

definitions.meaning: Abbey National, later Abbey, was a British bank, so this is its possessive
monastic churches and buildings of monks or nuns

explanation.definitionFit: The plural names monastic buildings, and with an apostrophe the British bank.

clue.text: Journalist, tired out, has nothing to hide

indicators.note: to hide means one piece is concealed inside another
out means the letters of the word are put out of order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An exhausted reporter with nothing to conceal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns TIRED into EDITR, and 'to hide' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper editor is a senior journalist.

clue.text: A French flat — that's odd!

parts.note: un is French for a
flat means level, even

explanation.surface: Someone surprised by an apartment in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven numbers are odd ones, a synonym.

clue.text: Origins of a wicker cradle?

parts.note: a place where willows used for wickerwork grow, punning on bed as both cradle and plot

explanation.definitionFit: Willow shoots for basketry grow in this plot, the source of wickerwork.

clue.text: A Spanish gent is a handsome fellow

parts.note: Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman described as good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was a youth of Greek myth famed for beauty, so any handsome man.

clue.text: Place bets wearing fabric tie

indicators.note: wearing means one piece is clothed by another, so goes inside it

parts.note: lint is a linen fabric used for dressings
to game is to gamble, place bets

explanation.surface: Gambling while dressed in a fabric necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is a band of tissue that ties bones together.

clue.text: A number of French pupils change direction at last

indicators.note: the final letter, a compass point, is swapped for another direction

parts.note: eleves is French for pupils

explanation.surface: Some French schoolchildren turn round at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: S (south) at the end of ELEVES becomes N (north).
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a cardinal number, one more than ten.

clue.text: It's a more unusual spray

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are arranged in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A remark that this spray is rarer than others.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that turns liquid into a fine spray, such as for perfume.
